card.occupation: New car sales executive at a franchised dealership on a retail park on the edge of town, on basic salary plus commission, with a rota that includes alternate Saturdays
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive and A-levels in Business Studies and English Language at a sixth form college in Basingstoke. She started a Business Management degree at Portsmouth but left after the first year because she 'wasn't learning anything I couldn't learn earning money'. Since then she has done manufacturer sales accreditation courses through work.
card.household: Lives with her husband Craig, 40, a self-employed electrician, in a three-bed semi on a 2000s estate in Chineham that they bought eight years ago. They have no children and a cocker spaniel called Dexter.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Basingstoke. Her dad was a warehouse manager at a distribution centre and her mum worked part-time as a dental receptionist. She is not religious and never has been, though she got married in a church 'because it looks better in the photos'. She thinks of herself as a no-nonsense, self-made, ordinary Hampshire person.
card.professional_persona: She is consistently near the top of the dealership's monthly sales board and makes sure everyone knows it. She is good at reading what a customer wants to hear and at closing. She will happily push finance add-ons and paint protection if it helps her figures, and she sees that as just the job. She gets impatient with colleagues she thinks are slow or soft, and she has had a couple of HR conversations about how bluntly she speaks to junior staff. She is not easily rattled by angry customers or bad months.
card.sports_persona: She goes to a gym on the retail park three times a week, mostly weights and the rowing machine, and tracks everything on her watch. She ran the Basingstoke Half once and mentions her time when running comes up. She watches the Formula 1 with Craig and likes the strategy and rivalries more than the cars.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest in galleries or theatre. She watches true crime documentaries and reality TV like The Traitors, which she says she would win, and she listens to podcasts in the car about business and people who've made money. She went to the Anvil once for a comedian and enjoyed it.
card.travel_persona: One or two holidays a year, usually all-inclusive somewhere hot such as Tenerife, Dubai or Turkey, picked partly on whether the hotel looks good. She likes upgrades and will complain at check-in to get one. Weekends away are city breaks such as Amsterdam or Barcelona with friends.
card.culinary_persona: Weeknight dinner is something quick, like chicken and rice or a fakeaway from a gym-friendly recipe account. Craig does most of the cooking. On Fridays they get a takeaway, usually Indian or Nando's. She likes the bottomless brunch places in town and says she 'doesn't do' fussy restaurants with tiny portions.
hobbies_and_interests: walking Dexter round the lakes at Chineham and in the woods
doing up the house, most recently a garden room
online shopping and reselling clothes on Vinted
skills: closing a sale and negotiating on price
working CRM systems and hitting targets
haggling with tradespeople and holiday companies
card.career_goals: Wants to become sales manager at the dealership, or at a bigger group if her current one doesn't promote her within a couple of years. She is open about wanting the money and the title and would move to a rival brand without much loyalty if the package were better.
card.voice: Confident, fairly fast and direct, in a standard south-east England accent that is unremarkable for Hampshire, with dropped t's in casual words ('a lo' of'). She says 'dinner' for the evening meal. She uses 'erm' occasionally when she's thinking, but less than most people, and sometimes says 'sort of' or 'to be fair'. She ends opinions with 'yeah?' or 'you know' as a check for agreement more than a real question. She is comfortable with silence and will let a pause sit rather than fill it, which can feel a bit like being sold to. She sometimes cuts in when she has guessed where a question is going.
card.typing: Quick and practical. She mostly capitalises the start of a sentence but often skips the full stop at the end. Her apostrophes are usually right but she drops them when rushing ('dont', 'im'). She uses short phrases instead of full sentences, the occasional 'tbh' or 'lol', and no emojis in a form. If she thinks a question is pointless she says so in a few words.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and polished at first, with good eye contact and the warmth of someone used to selling. She quickly works out whether a person is useful or interesting to her. If not, her attention drifts and she gets a bit dismissive. She gives strong opinions readily and doesn't soften disagreement much. Some people find her refreshingly straight and others find her a bit much.
small_things: Dexter rolling in fox poo on the morning walk
having a good month on the sales board
a delivery that hasn't turned up
being knackered after a Saturday shift
deeper_things: She and Craig have been going back and forth about whether to have kids, and she is privately fairly sure she doesn't want them
She doesn't get on with her younger sister, who she thinks has always been the favourite
She feels she has outgrown most of her school friends and doesn't mind that
She sometimes wonders whether she'd have earned more if she'd finished the degree, though she'd never admit regret to anyone
Money matters a lot to her because her parents were careful with it and she hated feeling like they couldn't afford things
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, framing her from mid-chest up, slightly off-centre to the left. Daylight comes from a window to her right and lights that side of her face, with the other side a little shadowed. She has an oval face, fair skin with light make-up, groomed eyebrows, and a confident closed-mouth half-smile. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted blonde with darker roots showing, straightened and tucked behind one ear. No glasses. She wears a navy fitted zip-up top with a small gym logo and small gold hoop earrings. Behind her is an open-plan kitchen-diner: grey gloss kitchen units, a white quartz-effect worktop with a coffee machine and a fruit bowl holding two bananas, a wall clock with metal numbers, and on the right edge of the frame part of a grey dog bed with a tennis ball in it.
